$comment: Canonical dispatch decision contract, shared by both runtimes.
The TypeScript enqueue gate owns the AUTHORING decision; the Python
dispatcher re-runs only the checks whose inputs can change between enqueue
and the provider call. Python does not reimplement the policy engine — it
reads the immutable snapshot and revalidates live state.
Both runtimes load this file and each has a parity test, so a block reason
or a lifecycle state cannot be added on one side alone.

lifecycle_states.deferred: policy says not now; deferred_until carries a deterministic next attempt
lifecycle_states.blocked: policy says never; terminal, and NOT a provider failure
lifecycle_states.failed: provider rejected or errored — a TRANSPORT failure, never a policy outcome

$preference_mapping_note: Which stored preference governs a (category, channel) pair. Declared here rather than asserted by string-matching either implementation, because both build these keys programmatically. Each runtime has a parity test that drives its own mapping function through this table.
$suppression_note: Only hard bounce and spam complaint suppress. A transient delivery failure is a retry concern, not a consent concern, and must not become permanent suppression.
